answer: A bonded-identity registry resists Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable deposit before trading. Like a saffron merchant staking rare stock, an agent posts collateral that is slashed if it cheats, so a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand deposits. A public atlas of reputation lets peers check whether an identity has a real timber of completed work behind it, not just a fresh name. The attacker thus pays linearly per fake identity and risks losing every bond if caught, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
